title: Application of  Orthohantavirus andesense  and  Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense  digital droplet RT-PCR assays in wastewater solids in the United States
content: Orthohantavirus andesense (Andes virus, ANDV) and Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense (Bundibugyo virus, BDBV) outbreaks in 2026 caused alarm in public health communities in the United States. In order to test whether wastewater surveillance could provide useful insights into the occurrence of infections in communities, we validated previously published hydrolysis probe-based droplet digital RT-PCR assays for ANDV and BDBV and then applied the assays retrospectively to wastewater samples from communities with and without individuals known to have been exposed to, or had potential to have been exposed to, other infected individuals. In silico and in vitro validation of the assays indicated that the assays are sensitive and specific to circulating viruses in 2026. ANDV and BDBV RNA were not detected at levels that were quantifiable in any sample. However, the ANDV assay detected RNA at concentrations above the limit of blank, in 26% of samples from sewersheds with exposed individuals and 0% of samples in the sewershed without known exposed individuals. However, no positive case was reported. The BDBV assay detected RNA at a low concentration, but above the limit of blank, in one sample from a sewershed with potentially exposed individuals; no positive case was reported in the United States. This work lays the groundwork for future application of these assays for wastewater surveillance for hantavirus and ebolavirus.
